drug_name: Sodium Sulfate and Potassium Sulfate (Bowel Prep Solution)
what_its_for: This medication is a bowel cleanser used to clean out your colon (large intestine) before a colonoscopy or other bowel procedure. It works by causing watery diarrhea to flush out stool and waste from your colon so your doctor can see clearly during the exam.
how_to_take: Mix the solution with water exactly as directed on the label or by your doctor. Drink the full amount of liquid required — this is very important for it to work properly. You will need to drink additional clear liquids (water, clear broth, clear juice) as instructed. Stay near a bathroom after taking this medication because it will cause you to have frequent, loose, watery bowel movements. Do NOT eat solid food during your prep period. Follow your doctor's specific instructions about when to start and stop eating.
dosing: Your doctor will give you a specific split-dose schedule, usually taken the evening before and the morning of your procedure, OR all in one evening. A typical split dose means you take the first half of the prep 5 to 6 hours before the second dose. Follow your prescription label exactly. Do not take more or less than prescribed. Make sure you finish all of the required liquid. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about your schedule.
missed_dose: If you forget a dose or do not finish your prep, contact your doctor or the procedure facility right away. An incomplete bowel prep may mean your colonoscopy needs to be rescheduled. Do NOT double up on doses without speaking to your doctor first.
storage: Store the unmixed solution or kit at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep it out of reach of children. Once mixed, check your product's label for specific storage instructions — some mixed solutions may need to be used within a certain number of hours. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat solid foods or high-fiber foods during your bowel prep period. Avoid red, purple, or orange colored drinks or foods, as these can look like blood during your exam. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or make important decisions right after your procedure, especially if you received sedation. Avoid taking other medications within 1 hour of taking this prep, as it may prevent your other medicines from being absorbed properly — ask your doctor or pharmacist about timing your regular medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe bloating or stomach pain, vomiting that prevents you from keeping the solution down, no bowel movements within 2 hours of starting the prep, signs of serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), severe dizziness or weakness, little to no urination, seizures, or irregular heartbeat. Also call your doctor if you have kidney disease, heart problems, or are on a low-sodium diet before starting this prep.
when_it_works: Most people start having bowel movements within 1 to 2 hours after taking the first dose. The prep is working when your bowel movements become clear or light yellow and watery with no solid pieces. This means your colon is clean and ready for the procedure. If your stool is not clear after completing the full prep, contact your doctor's office.
special_populations: Older adults and people with kidney disease, heart disease, or low fluid levels (dehydration) should use this medication with extra caution, as it can affect electrolyte levels in the blood. Pregnant women should talk to their doctor before using this medication. Children may need a different dose — always follow your doctor's guidance for pediatric patients. If you take medications for blood pressure, heart rhythm, or water pills (diuretics), talk to your doctor before your prep, as this medication can change your potassium and sodium levels.
